pressure in association with rapid weight gain in infancy, whereas other studies show no effect, or a protective effect (infants with
larger weight increments have lower blood pressure as adults). The degree to which rapid infant growth represents risk may depend
on whether it occurs in the context of recovery from fetal growth restriction and results in normalization of body weight versus
